thread:
Ivy: hey team, ivy here — first week. building the runtime from source in a WSL2 dev VM and hit a weird runtime link error when running unit tests: 'dlopen failed: cannot locate symbol __cudaRegisterFatBinary2 in libcuda.so.1'. build/link step completed fine. anyone seen the __cudaRegisterFatBinary2 missing symbol?

Carlos: welcome! that's typically a host vs container driver mismatch or a bad symlink to libcuda. can you paste `ldd build/libinfruntime.so` and `readlink -f /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1` from inside the test container?

Ivy: ldd shows libcuda.so.1 => /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so.1 (0x7f...), and readlink -f gives /mnt/wsl/Ubuntu-20.04/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (host path). the WSL host recently updated drivers. the symbol looks like a legacy registration API — maybe version mismatch?

Nia: that symbol is part of the CUDA driver ABI that the toolkit expects. If the container is resolving to a toolkit-provided libcuda (or one copied from elsewhere) but the host driver is different, you can get missing symbol errors. Since you're on WSL, also check that Docker Desktop is exposing the correct distro's libs. Quick checks: run `strings /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 | head` and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader` on the host.

Ivy: host nvidia-smi -> 535.54, container libcuda strings show 'CUDA Version: 12.2' and also some earlier SONAME notes. I think the container libcuda is stale (from copied toolkit). I tried replacing /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so.1 with a symlink to the host path but then the container fails to load it due to permission/namespace errors.

Carlos: for WSL we usually avoid copying libcuda into the image. Instead, run the tests with the host libs mounted: `docker run --gpus=all -v /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/:/host-lib:ro -e LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/host-lib ...` or use the nvidia-container-toolkit so the driver dir is mounted automatically. Also confirm the container hasn't baked in a different libc or toolkit that conflicts.

Ivy: mounting host dir worked — LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/host-lib made the tests hit the host libcuda and the missing symbol error disappeared. question: is there a recommended devcontainer setup for WSL users to avoid these one-off mounts?

Nia: we have a recommended .devcontainer in infra repo: ghcr.io/redwood/infr-dev:cuda12 (uses nvidia toolkit), plus a small wrapper script `dev/run-with-gpu.sh` that checks `nvidia-smi` then runs docker with the right flags. I'll DM the link. For CI we also add a pre-step that runs `python -c "import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1')"` in the runtime image and fails with a helpful message.

ops-bot: CI: added runtime preflight job suggestion to PR template.

Ivy: awesome — thanks y'all, switching my devcontainer to the infr-dev base and adding the wrapper script. super helpful :heart:
